title: Night Driving & Bad Weather
whatItIs: Darkness, rain, ice, fog, wind and low sun cut visibility or grip. See and be seen, slow down and leave far bigger gaps.

keyFacts.text: You MUST use headlights at night, except on roads with lit street lights.

keyFacts: Night (the hours of darkness): half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise.

keyFacts.text: You MUST use headlights when visibility is seriously reduced: generally under 100 metres.
You MUST NOT use fog lights unless visibility is seriously reduced, and MUST switch them off after.

keyFacts: Dazzled by oncoming headlights or bright sun? Slow down and, if necessary, stop.

keyFacts.text: In snow or ice you MUST clear all windows, and keep lights clean and number plates legible.

rows: Light steering? Ease off, slow gently
High gear, gentle; brake before bends

a.label: Fog lights
points: Only when visibility is seriously reduced
Can dazzle and hide your brake lights

b.label: Dipped headlights
points: At night in built-up areas and on dull days
MUST be used in seriously reduced visibility

onTheTest.question: The fog has cleared and visibility is well over 100 metres. Your pupil's rear fog lights are on. What now?
options: Leave them on to the end of the trip
Use the front fog lights only
onTheTest.why: Rule 236: you MUST switch fog lights off when visibility improves. They dazzle others and can hide your brake lights.

onTheTest.question: On an icy road, how much longer can stopping distances be than on a dry road?
onTheTest.why: Rules 126 and 230: stopping distances can be ten times greater on ice, so leave a gap up to ten times bigger.

traps: In fog, rear lights ahead give a false sense of security: keep a safe gap.
On ice, tyres make virtually no noise: light steering may mean you're losing grip.
Don't wear tinted glasses, lenses or visors at night if they restrict your vision.
